title: The Jalil: a hilltop tower with a theme park of facilities.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #481 | THE JALIL, PUNCAK JALIL
excerpt: A low-density project of about 430 units on a hilltop in landed Puncak Jalil, with a separate building just for facilities. Sean loves the setting and the corner unit with its extra suite, but warns of maintenance costs, rain in the corridors and two traffic bottlenecks.
takeaways: One of the only high-rises for kilometres, on a hilltop with open views and a separate facilities building.
A 1,070 sq ft corner unit resells for about RM560,000 and rents for about RM2,800 to RM3,200 furnished.
Big facilities mean big maintenance fees, and the open corridors will let the rain in.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: The Jalil puts about 430 units on a hilltop in a landed neighbourhood, and on its large plot builds a separate block just for facilities: a sea-themed children's play area with a water slide and a sand beach, a lap pool, a gym, a co-working space with meeting rooms, a theatre, karaoke and a community hall. Behind the towers, a landscaped garden with a bridge and a rain-fed jacuzzi runs past the garden units.

Every unit has at least two car parks. Sean viewed a 1,070 sq ft corner unit: a three-room wing with two bathrooms plus a separate suite with its own bathroom, so it can house a family, a home office or a studio to let.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It sits on Persiaran Puncak Jalil 1, between Bukit Jalil and Seri Kembangan, next to the field of SMK Taman Puncak Jalil and beside a petrol station and a power-line reserve kept green. Pavilion Bukit Jalil is 5 to 10 minutes away, and a large commercial area nearby has banks, clinics, daycares, hardware shops and eateries. There is no direct turn in from the far side, so drivers U-turn at the lights.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Subsale units list at about RM560,000, close to what buyers signed for three to four years ago, and fully furnished units ask about RM2,800 to RM3,200 a month. About 19 to 20 owners have signed a three-year arrangement with a nearby university paying about RM2,200 to RM2,300, but most owners Sean met live here with their families.

standout.title: A building just for facilities
standout.body: With so much land, the developer built a free-standing facilities block on the deck, its columns arranged for the spaces inside rather than for apartments above. It also stands between the road and the towers, shielding the homes from traffic noise.

pros: The setting: one of the only high-rises among landed homes, the tallest building on a hilltop, with views kept open by the power-line reserve, the highway setback and the school field next door, and good daylight and breezes as a result.

The architecture: the facilities block buffers the towers from road noise, the drop-off is at the quieter back, and there is far more than usual, from a viewing deck and rear garden with a rain-fed jacuzzi to a small hiking path. Corridors, lobbies and driveways are all generously sized.

The corner unit: an extra suite on top of a three-room home, laid out like a dual-key but sold for own stay. Rents of RM2,200 to RM3,200 are not bad, and Sean, who lives nearby, says he would buy one to live in.
cons: Getting in and out: evening jams from Sungai Besi via Pavilion, and a bottleneck turning in from Cyberjaya after Sierra 16. Once inside, the low-density area has everything, though the LRT is on the Bukit Jalil side and the malls are a drive away.

The facilities are overkill: he would cut a floor, gather the water areas in one place and keep the garden beside the corner units private. The pool overflow into the floor below needs better execution, and he estimates maintenance at about RM400 to RM500 per unit a month early on, possibly RM700 later.

Details: the big openings in the corridors and lift lobbies will let rain in, and enclosing them may breach fire rules. In the unit, air-conditioner blowers sit above the windows where curtains should go, and the compressors sit on the balcony rather than in the grilled ledge.

closing: Theme-park facilities with theme-park maintenance fees, ideal for families who know and love Puncak Jalil and spend a lot of time at home.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit after handover; prices and rents are from listings sites and owners as he quoted them, and the maintenance figure is his own estimate. Sean mentions that he lives nearby.
